title: Pins and skewers
intro: Line up two enemy pieces with a bishop, rook or queen. One of them is stuck, or one of them falls.

lessons.title: The pin
lessons.summary: A piece that cannot move because of what stands behind it.

steps.text: In a pin, a piece cannot move without exposing a more valuable piece behind it. Here your knight on c3 is pinned: if it moves, the bishop attacks your king, so it is not allowed to move at all.
A pinned piece is a sitting target. Here White's bishop pins the knight on c6 to Black's king.
Attack the pinned knight and win it.
steps.ifWrong: Attack the knight with something cheap: it cannot run away.
steps.ifRight: The knight cannot move, so it is lost.

feedback.b5c6: That trades your bishop for the knight. Attack it with the pawn instead and win it for free.

lessons.title: The skewer
lessons.summary: Attack the big piece; take the one behind.

steps.text: A skewer is a pin turned around: the more valuable piece stands in front. When it moves away, you capture the piece behind it. Watch the bishop check the king.
The king must step out of check, and then the bishop takes the queen on e8.
Skewer the king and the rook.
steps.hint: Check the king along the 7th row.
steps.ifWrong: Check the king on the row it shares with the rook.
steps.ifRight: The king moves, and the rook on h7 falls.
